# pidginhost_floating_ip (Resource)

A floating IPv4 or IPv6 address that the authorized servers can take over.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pidginhost_floating_ip" "lb" {
  version     = 4
  label       = "lb"
  reverse_dns = "lb.example.com"

  authorized_server_ids = [
    pidginhost_server.lb1.id,
    pidginhost_server.lb2.id,
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `version` (Number) IP version: 4 or 6. Changing it replaces the address.

### Optional

- `authorized_server_ids` (Set of String) IDs of the servers allowed to use the address. The set is authoritative: servers authorized outside it lose their authorization.
- `label` (String) Label of the address. The API cannot rename it, so changing it replaces the address.
- `reverse_dns` (String) Reverse DNS (PTR) name of the address.

### Read-Only

- `address` (String) The IP address.
- `gateway` (String) Gateway of the address.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the object in the PidginHost API.
- `prefix` (Number) Prefix length of the address network.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a floating IP by "<version>/<id>", since IPv4 and IPv6 addresses have separate IDs.
terraform import pidginhost_floating_ip.lb 4/12345
```
